set.body:
Journey: Bring in. Track: engine and console.

Outcome
Creating the first dataset in a fresh instance never asks anyone for a UUID. The custodian is chosen by name.

Why
Dataset creation recognises a custodian only if some existing dataset already carries that UUID, and the form asks the researcher to type it. A new instance therefore needs operator setup outside the product before its first deposit. The operator create command bypasses the check, which is how the demo seed works.

Acceptance
1. An operator registers a custodian with a stable identifier and a display name before its first dataset.
2. The create-dataset form defaults to the only eligible custodian, lists names when there are several, and explains an empty list.
3. Existing custodian identifiers are backfilled without merging or guessing. Existing releases keep their identities, and the historical compatibility corpus passes.
4. The study page shows the custodian's name.

Not in scope
Custody transfer workflows. Custody across institutions.

Start from
- modules/postgres/src/main/scala/sanctity/postgres/PostgresOrganizationCatalog.scala line 138.
- modules/http/src/main/resources/sanctity/ui/app.js line 418, the Custodian ID field of the creation form.

Evidence
Tests for a clean bootstrap and for an existing catalog. The first deposit in the SHARE5 rehearsal.
set.title: IN5: Named custodians on first deposit (was ARC01)
